subject: physics_2
question_text: What do you understand by the terms 'focus' and 'principal focus' in the context of lenses?

verification.note: From FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students (physics section), Ch.2 Ray Optics and Optical Instruments, printed p.10 — Section A, 2 marks. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. PRINTED-ANSWER CORRECTION: the book writes that a beam tilted to the principal axis meets at 'a point on principal axis' and calls the emerging rays 'reflected'. Both are wrong for a lens: the rays REFRACT, and a tilted parallel beam meets OFF the axis, at a point in the FOCAL PLANE through F. This card writes the focal-plane statement and records the book's version in the step's why.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Ray Optics and Optical Instruments · 2 marks

steps.label: Principal focus
lines: A beam parallel to the principal axis, after
appears to diverge from (concave lens) a
fixed point on the principal axis. This point
is the principal focus F of the lens.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The defining beam is the one parallel to the principal axis; F sits ON the axis.
steps.why: One special beam — the one parallel to the principal axis — defines one fixed point F. Saying converges for a convex lens and appears to diverge for a concave lens covers both lenses in one definition.
common_mistakes: Leaving out appears to diverge, which loses the concave-lens case.
Calling any meeting point a principal focus. F is defined only by the beam parallel to the principal axis.

recall.must_convey: That rays parallel to the principal axis converge to, or appear to diverge from, a fixed point on the axis called the principal focus.
accept: rays parallel to the principal axis meet at the principal focus on the axis
parallel beam converges to F or appears to diverge from F
principal focus is where the axis-parallel beam focuses
axis ki parallel rays anni F daggara kalustayi
reject: a tilted beam meets in the focal plane

steps.memory_tip: Principal focus goes with the principal axis: axis-parallel beam → point ON the axis.

steps.label: Focus of a tilted beam
lines: If the parallel beam makes a small angle with
the principal axis, the refracted rays meet
at a point OFF the axis, in the focal plane —
the plane through F perpendicular to the
axis. That point is the focus of that beam.

lines.text: Parallel to axis → F · tilted → focal plane

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The tilted beam's meeting point is OFF the axis, in the focal plane through F.
steps.why: The book prints that the tilted beam meets at a point on the principal axis and calls the rays reflected. Both are slips: a lens refracts, and only the axis-parallel beam focuses at F on the axis — a tilted beam focuses off the axis, in the focal plane through F.
common_mistakes: Writing that the tilted beam also meets on the principal axis. It meets off the axis, in the focal plane.
Writing reflected for a lens. A lens refracts light.
Treating focus and principal focus as the same point. Every beam has a focus; only the axis-parallel beam's focus is the principal focus.

recall.must_convey: That a parallel beam tilted to the axis meets at a point off the axis in the focal plane, and that point is called the focus of that beam.
accept: a tilted parallel beam meets at a point in the focal plane
the focus of a slanted beam is off the axis in the plane through F
tilted beam focuses in the focal plane not on the axis
angle tho vachina beam focal plane lo focus avutundi
reject: rays parallel to the principal axis meet at the principal focus

steps.memory_tip: One plane holds every focus: the focal plane through F. On-axis beam → F itself; tilted beam → another point of that plane.

insider_note: The whole distinction is one word each: principal focus ON the axis, focus of a tilted beam OFF the axis in the focal plane.
